mainTopic: Which wrong intentions disqualify a קרבן, and the source and limits of רבי יהודה's view on intent to leave it over or take it out
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's list of wrong intentions during שחיטה that leave a קרבן כשר. The משנה then gives the rule behind the list: only חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו, and שלא לשמן (for a פסח or חטאת) disqualify. The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's source for disqualifying intent to leave the קרבן over or take it out. רבי אלעזר points to the extra wording 'לא יניח' and defends it against a ברייתא that seems to use that פסוק up. The גמרא then suggests that רבי יהודה's reason is logic: intending is like doing. It explains why he still does not argue on the other cases, because in them the act itself would not ruin the קרבן. To explain why he ignores intent to put blood inside the היכל, the גמרא says he requires a 'threefold place'. Sources about רבי יהודה conflict on this point, and the גמרא settles it by saying two תנאים report his view differently. Finally it begins a new question about a חטאת slaughtered in the south, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: More wrong intentions that do not disqualify the offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of improper intentions during שחיטה. It rules that in all of these cases the קרבן stays כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered intending to put blood meant for inside the היכל on the outside altar, or blood meant for outside on the inside; or intending that impure people will eat it or offer it; or that uncircumcised people will eat it or offer it; or intending to break the bones of the פסח, to eat it half-roasted, or to mix its blood with the blood of disqualified קרבנות, the offering is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a long list of wrong intentions a person might have while slaughtering. It says none of them make the קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item here is a real wrong act. Some of them would even ruin the קרבן if actually done. But merely intending to do them at the time of שחיטה does not affect the קרבן's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning the inner altar in the היכל
Outside, meaning the outer altar in the courtyard
Ritually impure people
Uncircumcised people, who may not eat or offer קדשים
Half-roasted meat, which is forbidden for the פסח
Fit, valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think these acts are allowed! The משנה only says that intending them during שחיטה does not disqualify the קרבן. Actually doing them is still forbidden.

phrases.english: [or to place the blood meant for] inside — outside;
and the blood that is placed outside — inside;
that impure people will eat it; that impure people will offer it;
that uncircumcised people will eat it; and that uncircumcised people will offer it;
to break the bones of the Paschal offering;
to eat from it half-roasted;
or to mix its blood with the blood of unfit offerings — it is fit.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrong intentions about where blood is placed, who eats or offers the קרבן, breaking the פסח's bones, eating it half-roasted, or mixing its blood do not disqualify the offering.

steps.title: Only certain intentions disqualify an offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains why all the previous cases are כשר. Only three kinds of intent can disqualify a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For intent only disqualifies when it is intent for beyond its time or outside its place, and, for the פסח and the חטאת, intent of not for their sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the general rule behind the list. Only a few specific intentions have the power to disqualify a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disqualifying intentions are חוץ לזמנו (eating or burning it after its time), חוץ למקומו (eating or burning it outside its place), and שלא לשמן. The last one only disqualifies a פסח and a חטאת. Any other wrong intention, like the ones just listed, has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent during the service
Beyond its time, intending to eat or burn it after its allowed time
Outside its place, intending to eat or burn it outside its allowed area
Not for their sake, intending it as a different kind of קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: Only חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו, and שלא לשמן (for a פסח or חטאת) are disqualifying intentions. Every other bad intention leaves the קרבן כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for all of מסכת זבחים. It sets clear limits on the power of מחשבה.

phrases.english: For intent does not disqualify
except intent of beyond its time or outside its place,
and the Paschal offering and the sin offering, intended not for their sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rulings in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only intent of חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו, and שלא לשמן (for a פסח or חטאת) disqualifies an offering.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why רבי יהודה disqualifies the קרבן. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, רבי יהודה ruled that intending to leave the blood or the sacrificial parts until the next day, or to take them outside, disqualifies the קרבן. The חכמים say it is כשר. That fits the משנה's closing rule, since this intent is not on the list. So the גמרא wants to know what source רבי יהודה has.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי יהודה's ruling that intent to leave the blood overnight disqualifies the offering.

steps.title: An extra verse teaches about intending to leave it over
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says there are two פסוקים forbidding leaving the meat until morning. Since one is extra, it teaches that even the intent to leave it over matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Two פסוקים are written about נותר. One says, 'You shall not leave any of it until morning,' and one says, 'He shall not leave any of it until morning.' If one is not needed for the act of leaving, apply it to the intent of leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by pointing to an extra פסוק. רבי יהודה reads that extra פסוק as being about intent to leave it over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on leaving the קרבן until morning is already stated once. The second פסוק looks unnecessary, so it is used for something new: disqualifying the intent to leave it overnight. This uses the method of אם אינו ענין, where a פסוק that is not needed for its plain topic is moved to a related one.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover sacrificial meat past its time
If it is not needed for this topic, apply it to another
Intent to leave it over

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Two verses are written about leftover meat;
one verse says:
"You shall not leave any of it until morning,"
and one verse says:
"He shall not leave any of it until morning";
if it is not needed for the matter of leaving it over,
apply it to the matter of intent to leave it over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי בְּנוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק about not leaving the meat until morning is extra, so רבי יהודה uses it to forbid the intent of leaving it overnight.

steps.title: That verse is needed for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: רבי יהודה needs the פסוק of 'לא יניח' for a teaching in a ברייתא about the תודה, so it is not really extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יהודה use this פסוק for this? He needs it for what was taught: 'And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving.' From here we learned that a תודה is eaten for a day and a night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4. It says the 'extra' פסוק is actually used for another law, and it starts quoting a ברייתא that shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's whole answer rests on the second פסוק being unneeded. The גמרא points to a ברייתא that reads ויקרא 7:15 for the laws of the תודה, starting with its eating time of a day and a night. If the פסוק is busy with that teaching, it is not free to teach about intent. The ברייתא continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it come for this purpose?
He needs it for something else
As was taught in a ברייתא
Thanksgiving offering
For one day and the following night

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda —
does this verse come for this purpose?!
He needs this verse
for that which was taught:
"And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:15, the same פסוק that says 'לא יניח ממנו עד בקר'.

phrases.english: we learned regarding a thanks offering
that it is eaten for a day and a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַאי קְרָא לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the פסוק 'לא יניח ממנו עד בקר' is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא uses ויקרא 7:15 to teach the laws of the תודה, so the פסוק is not free to teach intent of leaving it over.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: every word of the תודה פסוק is used up
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from each word of the פסוק that many other offerings and breads are also eaten for only a day and a night. All of them fall under 'לא יניח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animals exchanged for a תודה, its offspring, and its substitutes: where do we learn they are eaten for only a day and a night? The פסוק says 'And the flesh.' A חטאת and an אשם: where do we learn this? The פסוק says 'sacrifice.' Where do we learn to include the שלמים of a נזיר and the שלמים of פסח? The פסוק says 'his peace offerings.' The breads of the תודה and the loaves and wafers of the נזיר: where do we learn this? The פסוק says 'his offering.' For all of them I read the words 'he shall not leave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the ברייתא it brought in the last step as its challenge. The ברייתא uses each word of the פסוק to add more offerings to the one-day eating rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word, such as 'ובשר', 'זבח', 'שלמיו' and 'קרבנו', adds another group of offerings. The ברייתא then applies 'לא יניח' to all of them. So 'לא יניח' seems busy teaching that these offerings may not be left overnight, and it is not extra for רבי אלעזר's teaching about intent.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal exchanged for a lost תודה, brought in its place
An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן; it also becomes holy
The פסוק teaches, introducing the source
To include, to add more cases
Loaves and wafers, breads brought with a קרבן

phrases.english: Exchanged animals, offspring, and substitutes: from where do we know?
phrases.notes: All of these are connected to a תודה. The question is how we know they are also eaten for only a day and a night.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And the flesh.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:15. The extra 'and' adds these cases.

phrases.english: A sin offering and a guilt offering: from where?
The verse states: 'Sacrifice.'

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת שַׁלְמֵי נָזִיר וְשַׁלְמֵי פֶסַח?
phrases.english: And from where do we include the peace offering of a nazirite and the peace offering of Passover?
The verse states: 'His peace offerings.'

phrases.aramaic: לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה, וְחַלּוֹת וּרְקִיקִים שֶׁבְּנָזִיר – מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: The breads of the thanks offering, and the loaves and wafers of the nazirite: from where?
The verse states: 'His offering.'
For all of them I read 'He shall not leave.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲלִיפִין, וְולָדוֹת, תְּמוּרוֹת – מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 5 as the basis of the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that 'לא יניח' is an extra פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses 'לא יניח' to apply the overnight rule to many offerings, so the words are not free to teach about intent.

steps.title: The special wording 'לא יניח' is still free to teach about intent
steps.stepSummary: The תורה could have written 'לא תותירו'. Its choice of 'לא יניח' points to the intent to leave the meat over.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'You shall not leave over.' Why does it say 'He shall not leave'? If it is not needed for actually leaving the meat over, apply it to the intent to leave it over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. The ברייתא's teachings could have been taught with the usual wording 'לא תותירו', so the different wording 'לא יניח' is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only needs some phrase saying 'do not leave it until morning.' Since the תורה used an unusual word, 'יניח', that word has room for a further teaching. Because the actual leaving over is already covered, the word is applied to the intent to leave it over.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall not leave over, the wording in another פסוק
If it is not needed for its own topic, apply it to another
Intent to leave the meat over

steps.whatToRemember: The plain rule against leaving the meat over could have been written with 'לא תותירו'. The special word 'לא יניח' is used for intent, which supports רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say: 'You shall not leave over.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:30 uses this wording for the same kind of rule.

phrases.english: Why does it say 'He shall not leave'?
If it is not needed for the matter of leaving over,
apply it to the matter of intent to leave over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: the unusual word choice frees the פסוק for a new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא יניח' is fully used by the ברייתא for the overnight rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The overnight rule could have used 'לא תותירו', so 'לא יניח' teaches that intent to leave over disqualifies.

steps.title: What is the source for intent to take the parts out?
steps.stepSummary: The extra-פסוק source only covers intent to leave the parts overnight. It does not explain רבי יהודה's view about intent to take them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for intent to leave over. But for intent to take out, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty. רבי יהודה also holds that intent to take the parts out of their area disqualifies, and the פסוק of 'לא יניח' says nothing about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's answer gives a source only for leaving over. The גמרא now asks what source covers taking out. This sets up the next part of the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well, granted for this case
To take out, here meaning intent to take the parts out of their proper area
What can be said? The source is still missing

phrases.english: This works well for intent to leave over,
but for intent to take out, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח לְהָנִיחַ, לְהוֹצִיא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 7 but points out it covers only half of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's source as a full explanation of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה also disqualifies a קרבן for intent to take its parts out, and 'לא יניח' cannot teach that.

steps.title: Another challenge: רבי יהודה's reason is logic, not a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a further problem for רבי אלעזר: רבי יהודה's view seems to come from logic, not from an extra פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the reason of רבי יהודה is logical reasoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second attack on רבי אלעזר's claim that רבי יהודה learns his rule from an extra פסוק. It says רבי יהודה's reason is simple logic, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said רבי יהודה needs a פסוק to teach that the intent to leave meat over disqualifies. If רבי יהודה's real reason is logic, the whole search for a פסוק was unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an additional challenge
The reason
Logical reasoning, as opposed to a פסוק

phrases.english: And furthermore, the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is logical reasoning!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבָרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent objection to the one in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that רבי יהודה's rule comes from an extra פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is based on logic, there is no need for a פסוק source.

steps.title: The ברייתא: intending is like doing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה arguing from logic: just as leaving the meat over disqualifies, so does intending to leave it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יהודה said to the חכמים: Don't you agree that if he actually left it until the next day, it is disqualified? So too, if he intended to leave it until the next day, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its point with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים using pure logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה compares intention to action. Since everyone agrees that actually leaving it over disqualifies, he reasons that planning to do so should disqualify too. No פסוק is mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Agree, concede
He left it over until the next day
He intended, had in mind

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the חכמים who argue with him in the משנה.

phrases.english: Do you not agree
that if he left it until the next day, it is disqualified?
So too, if he intended to leave it until the next day, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source proving the claim of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's view is based on logic
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה compares intention to action

steps.title: If it's logic, he should disagree about everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if רבי יהודה uses logic, he should disagree with every case in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is רבי יהודה's reason really logic?! Then let רבי יהודה also disagree about all the other cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the idea that רבי יהודה's reason is logic. If it were, he would apply it to every intention in the משנה, not only to leaving it overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists many intentions that do not disqualify an offering, and רבי יהודה argues only about leaving it over and taking it out. If his rule were simply that intention equals action, he should argue on all of them. Since he does not, maybe his source really is a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him disagree
In all of them

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבָרָא הוּא?!
phrases.english: But is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda logic?!
Then let Rabbi Yehuda also disagree in all of them!
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the other intentions listed in the משנה that the חכמים say do not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבָרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 9-10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה's view is based on logic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A logical principle (intention equals action) should apply to every case in the משנה, yet רבי יהודה argues only about some.

steps.title: Breaking the bones or eating it half-roasted doesn't ruin the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: in the other cases, even doing the act wouldn't ruin the offering, so intending it can't either. First example: the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: About which case should he disagree? About intending to break the bones of the פסח or to eat it half-roasted? Even if he actually did it, would the offering itself become disqualified?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer step 11 by going through the משנה's cases one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's logic only works where the action itself would ruin the offering. Breaking a פסח bone or eating it half-roasted is a sin, but it does not make the offering itself disqualified. So intending those acts cannot disqualify it either.

keyTerms.meaning: In which?
Partially roasted, not fully cooked
The offering itself
Become disqualified

phrases.english: In which case should he disagree?
In one who intends to break the bones of the פסח
and to eat from it partially roasted?
Is the offering itself disqualified?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic would make רבי יהודה disqualify every intention in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: His logic only applies where the act itself would ruin the offering.

steps.title: Impure or uncircumcised people eating or offering it
steps.stepSummary: The same answer applies to intending that טמאים or ערלים eat or offer it: even if that happened, the offering itself is not disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: On condition that impure people eat it or that impure people offer it: would the offering itself become disqualified?! That uncircumcised people eat it or uncircumcised people offer it: would the offering itself become disqualified?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues through more cases from the משנה and gives the same answer each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act these intentions describe does not make the offering itself פסול. Since the act wouldn't disqualify it, רבי יהודה's 'intention is like action' logic gives no reason to disqualify here.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that, with the intent that
Ritually impure people
Uncircumcised people
That they will offer it on the מזבח

phrases.english: On condition that impure people will eat it
and that impure people will offer it
Is the offering itself disqualified?!
That uncircumcised people will eat it and uncircumcised people will offer it
Is the offering itself disqualified?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 12's answer to more cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: These acts would not ruin the offering itself, so intending them does not either.

steps.title: Another version: it's not up to him
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the answer for the טמאים and ערלים cases: whether others eat or offer it is not in his control.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: Is it in his power?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to explain why רבי יהודה does not disagree about the טמאים and ערלים cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the reason is not that the act wouldn't ruin the offering. It is that what other people will do is up to them, not him, so his intention about it carries no weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version
Is it in his power?

phrases.english: Another version: Is it in his power?!
phrases.notes: Whether impure or uncircumcised people eat or offer it depends on them, not on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for the cases in step 13.
steps.terutzMaskana: An intention about acts that depend on other people is meaningless.

steps.title: Mixing with unfit blood: blood doesn't cancel blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה doesn't disagree about intending to mix the blood with unfit blood, because he holds that blood does not nullify blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Intending to mix their blood with the blood of unfit offerings: רבי יהודה follows his own view, since he says blood does not nullify blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another case from the משנה using a rule רבי יהודה holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, if the good blood were actually mixed with unfit blood, it would not be cancelled out and the offering would still be valid. Since the act wouldn't ruin it, the intention doesn't either.

keyTerms.meaning: To mix
Unfit offerings
Following his own reasoning
Blood does not nullify other blood

phrases.english: To mix their blood with the blood of unfit offerings
Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning, as he says:
Blood does not nullify blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: אֵין דָּם מְבַטֵּל דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues answering step 11 with another case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: רבי יהודה follows his own known view
steps.terutzMaskana: Actually mixing wouldn't disqualify according to רבי יהודה, so intending to mix doesn't either.

steps.title: Wrong spot on the מזבח still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה doesn't disagree about intending to put the blood above or below the line in the wrong spot, because he holds that the wrong place still counts as its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Intending to place blood meant for above the line below it, or blood meant for below it above it: רבי יהודה follows his own view, since he says even the wrong place is considered its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with the last case and again shows that רבי יהודה's own view explains why he doesn't argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, blood actually placed in the wrong spot still makes the offering acceptable. Since doing it wouldn't ruin the offering, intending it doesn't either. This completes the answer: his logic of 'intention like action' never disqualifies in these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Above the red line on the מזבח
Below the red line
Not in its proper place
We call it, it counts as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's 'intention is like action' logic only disqualifies where the act itself would ruin the offering. That is why he argues only about leaving it over or taking it out, and not about the other cases in the משנה.

phrases.english: To place those meant to be placed above, below
phrases.notes: "Above" and "below" mean above or below the red line around the מזבח.

phrases.english: or those meant below, above
Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning, as he says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לִמְקוֹמוֹ נָמֵי מְקוֹמוֹ קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Even not in its place, we also call it its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא לִמְקוֹמוֹ נָמֵי מְקוֹמוֹ קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case-by-case answer to step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: רבי יהודה follows his own known view
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood placed in the wrong spot still works for רבי יהודה, so intending it doesn't disqualify.

steps.title: Why not disagree about blood placed in the wrong area?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה does not also disagree about intending to put inside-blood outside, or outside-blood inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יהודה disagree about blood that belongs inside but was placed outside, and blood that belongs outside but was placed inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its line of questions. It suggests one more case where רבי יהודה should have said the wrong intention ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15-16 explained why רבי יהודה stays quiet about mixing blood and about the line on the מזבח. Here the case is different, because the תורה says outright that a חטאת whose blood was brought inside is פסול. So the act really does ruin it, and the intention should too.

keyTerms.meaning: blood that is meant to be put inside the היכל, on the inner מזבח
blood that is meant to be put outside, on the outer מזבח in the courtyard
so let him disagree

phrases.english: And let him disagree about blood that is placed inside
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רבי יהודה. 'Inside' means inside the היכל, the building past the courtyard.

phrases.english: that one placed outside,
and blood placed outside that one placed inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as before, now asked about a new case: the wrong area, inside or outside.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רבי יהודה does not count intending to put blood in the wrong area (inside or outside) as disqualifying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 12 set the rule that if the act would ruin the קרבן, the intention should too. Bringing a חטאת's blood inside does ruin it, so the intention should as well.

steps.title: A disqualifying place must serve blood, meat, and sacrificial parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that an intention about a wrong place only ruins a קרבן if that place works for all three: blood, meat, and אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: we need a place that is 'threefold': for blood, for meat, and for the sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה has a special condition for wrong-place intentions. The place he intends must be one that works for all three parts of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the עזרה fits this, because back when private altars (במות) were allowed, blood, meat and אימורין were all offered or eaten there. The היכל only ever gets blood. No meat is eaten there and no אימורין are burned there, so intending to use it does not ruin the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'threefold' place, one that works for blood, meat, and sacrificial parts
the parts of the קרבן burned on the מזבח
he holds

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a condition for רבי יהודה that the next steps will test against other sources.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה holds:
we need a place that is threefold –
phrases.notes: He means the place you intend must count for all three parts of the קרבן, not just one.

phrases.english: for blood, for meat, and for the sacrificial parts.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בָּעֵינַן מְקוֹם שֶׁיְּהֵא מְשׁוּלָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a condition that the case in question does not meet.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wrong place that would ruin the קרבן by the act should also ruin it by intention.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, only a place that works for blood, meat and אימורין counts. The היכל does not qualify.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה disqualifies blood that went inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the threefold idea. In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה learns from 'דבר רע' that a חטאת whose blood went inside is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold this idea? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: 'an evil thing' adds here a חטאת slaughtered in the south and a חטאת whose blood entered inside, that they are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really holds the 'threefold place' rule. It brings a ברייתא where he disqualifies a חטאת because of the היכל, a place that is not threefold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Whose blood entered inside' is understood here as slaughtering with the intention of bringing the blood inside. If so, an intention about the היכל does ruin the קרבן for רבי יהודה. That clashes with step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: 'an evil thing' (דברים 17:1), the words רבי יהודה learns from
the פסוק added, included more cases
the south side of the עזרה, while a חטאת must be slaughtered in the north

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַאי סְבָרָא?!
phrases.english: And does רבי יהודה hold this reasoning?!
But it is taught: רבי יהודה says:
'An evil thing' – it included here
a חטאת that one slaughtered in the south
and a חטאת whose blood entered inside, that it is פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַאי סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה requires a threefold place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי יהודה disqualifying a חטאת connected to the היכל, which is not threefold. So he does not seem to require the threefold condition.

steps.title: A משנה that seems to show רבי יהודה does hold the threefold idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back from the other side. A משנה shows רבי יהודה is lenient about blood brought inside: it is פסול only if done on purpose, and only once he actually atoned with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יהודה not hold of 'three'? But we learned in a משנה that רבי יהודה said: if he brought it in by mistake, it is כשר. That means if on purpose, it is פסול. And we hold that this is only where he atoned with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the doubt it just raised. It cites a משנה showing that רבי יהודה is quite lenient about the היכל, which fits the threefold rule. The two sources now seem to pull against each other, and the גמרא is setting up a resolution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, blood that was brought inside is not automatically ruined. It is פסול only if brought in on purpose, and only after he actually put it on the inner מזבח. That is hard to square with the ברייתא of step 19, which disqualifies a mere intention about the היכל. The next steps sharpen this and then resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'three', here meaning the threefold-place rule
by mistake
on purpose
where he atoned, meaning he actually put the blood on the inner מזבח
we hold, it is established for us

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final answer. The גמרא has now set two sources about רבי יהודה against each other, and step 22 resolves the clash.

phrases.english: And does רבי יהודה not hold of 'three'?!
phrases.notes: 'Three' refers back to the threefold place from step 18.

phrases.english: But we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה said:
If he brought it in by mistake – it is כשר.
phrases.notes: He brought the blood into the היכל.

phrases.english: That implies: on purpose – it is פסול;
and we hold this is where he atoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the challenge of step 19 with a source on the other side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The doubt raised in step 19 that רבי יהודה does not hold the threefold rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows רבי יהודה disqualifies blood brought into the היכל only in a narrow case: on purpose, and after it was actually put on the inner מזבח. This suggests he does not treat the היכל as a place that easily ruins a קרבן, which fits the threefold rule.

steps.title: If actually bringing blood inside is treated leniently, just thinking about it should be even more lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge with a קל וחומר. In the משנה, blood that was really brought inside is פסול only if he atoned with it. So a mere thought of bringing it inside should surely not make the קרבן פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think about it: there, where he really brought the blood inside, it is פסול only if he atoned with it, and not if he didn't. Here, where he only thought about bringing it inside, shouldn't it surely be fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge it started in step 20. It uses a קל וחומר to show that the lenient משנה, which fits the 'threefold place' rule, contradicts the ברייתא of step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows רבי יהודה is lenient even when the blood was actually brought inside, unless he atoned with it. A mere thought is weaker than a real act, so a thought of bringing it inside should surely not disqualify, exactly as the threefold rule of step 18 says. That clashes with the ברייתא in step 19, where רבי יהודה disqualifies a חטאת whose blood was meant to go inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, think about it (opens a 'how much more so' argument)
He atoned, meaning he actually did the blood service with it
Thinking, having an intention (מחשבה)
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'There' means blood that was really carried inside. 'Here' means blood that was only thought about being brought inside during the service.

phrases.english: Now, if there
where he actually brought it inside,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: if he atoned with it, yes, it is פסול,
if he did not atone, no, it is not פסול;
here, where he only thought about it,
is it not all the more so fine?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from the משנה begun in step 20 by drawing out its קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 19, which has רבי יהודה disqualifying a חטאת whose blood was meant to be brought inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real act is stronger than a thought. If the real act of bringing blood inside disqualifies only when he atoned with it, a mere thought of bringing it inside should surely not disqualify. That contradicts the ברייתא of step 19.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי יהודה's view differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a disagreement between two תנאים about what רבי יהודה held. One source holds he is strict, and the other holds he is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they argue about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction between the ברייתא (step 19) and the משנה (steps 20-21). It says they reflect two different reports of רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make the two sources fit together. It accepts that they disagree and splits them between two תנאים who quote רבי יהודה differently. So the 'threefold place' explanation can stand according to one of those reports.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים who disagree
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: The 'threefold place' explanation of רבי יהודה works according to one report of his view, which is lenient about intending to bring blood inside. Another תנא, in the ברייתא of 'דבר רע', reports him as stricter.

phrases.english: There are two תנאים
and they disagree about the view of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 19-21 by splitting the sources between two תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תרי תנאי: the conflicting sources reflect two different reports of the same תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה both quote רבי יהודה, so they should agree. Yet the strict ברייתא seems to disprove the 'threefold place' idea, while the lenient משנה supports it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים report רבי יהודה differently. The 'threefold place' explanation follows one of them.

steps.title: Opening a new question about a חטאת slaughtered in the south
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge, asking whether רבי יהודה really holds a certain law about a חטאת slaughtered in the south. The rest of the question continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יהודה really hold that a חטאת that was slaughtered in the south...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts a new question about רבי יהודה's view of a חטאת slaughtered in the wrong place, and the full question comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה, so the south is a wrong place for it. The words 'וסבר רבי יהודה' show surprise: the גמרא is about to question a ruling credited to רבי יהודה about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he hold? (opens a surprised challenge)
South (here, the southern side of the עזרה)
He slaughtered it

phrases.english: And does רבי יהודה hold:
a חטאת that one slaughtered in the south —
phrases.notes: A חטאת is supposed to be slaughtered in the north, so the south is the wrong spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the contradiction, the גמרא goes back to the other case in the ברייתא of step 19, a חטאת slaughtered in the south, and starts to question it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the ברייתא of step 19 that, according to רבי יהודה, a חטאת slaughtered in the south is פסול (the full question continues on the next amud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The surprised wording 'וסבר' signals that the גמרא finds this ruling hard to accept for רבי יהודה. The full reasoning comes in the next part of the text.
